blocks.body:
### Resources
▪ Each player must have a Dominatus deck.
### Warmaster
▪ The Warhammer Event organiser is the Warmaster.
▪ At the start of each campaign phase, the Warmaster can select that phase's Location card, instead of rolling.
▪ The Warmaster can require a player to change their Alliance (see Muster Armies).
### Changes to the End of Campaign Phase
▪ The **Acquire Relics** step and the **Discard** step at the end of each campaign phase are resolved at the Determine Mission step of the first battle in the next campaign phase, instead of as described in the Dominatus deck.
▪ The **Fresh Supplies** and **Test of Mettle** location bonuses are resolved at the Determine Mission step of the first battle in the next campaign phase, instead of as described in the Dominatus deck.
▪ The **Auspicious Augury** location bonus is resolved as described in the Dominatus deck, but we recommend that each player does so in the presence of a player from another Alliance.
blocks.title: Event Guidance

blocks.body: Excluding Core CP, each player can gain a maximum of 1CP per battle round (including the CP gained when a player discards an active Secondary Mission card).
blocks.title: Generating Command Points

blocks.body:
The battle follows the Event Companion's mission sequence, with these changes:
▪ **1. Muster Armies** — once they have mustered their army, a player selects one Force Disposition card available to them and one **Alliance** as described in the Dominatus deck, and records those on their roster.
▪ **2. Determine Mission** — read aloud the war zone rules from your Location card; Agendas and Declining Agendas as in the Dominatus deck (when declining, Primary Missions are determined by comparing Force Disposition cards). Whether players attempt Agendas or not, the players' Force Disposition cards are used to determine a layout.
▪ **7. Declare Battle Formations** — players also secretly note down up to 3 Upgrade cards they have earned during the campaign, and which friendly unit each is given to until the end of the battle (a unit cannot have more than one Upgrade card).
▪ **14. Determine Victor** — each player scores 10VP if their army is painted to a Battle Ready standard. Maximum VP: Primary Mission 45VP (up to 15VP per battle round); Secondary Missions 45VP (up to 15VP per battle round, and a maximum of 20VP per Fixed Secondary Mission card); Battle Ready army 10VP. Once a victor is determined, Agenda Achieved cards and Upgrade draws are resolved as in the Dominatus deck.
blocks.title: Event Mission Sequence

blocks.body: In a Dominatus event, players are paired with a player from another Alliance; beyond that, pair as the Event Companion recommends — first by record, then by win path, then randomly.
blocks.title: Pairings

event.intro: Guidance from GW's Warhammer Dominatus Event Companion for running an organised Dominatus event with the Dominatus deck and the most recent Chapter Approved Mission Deck. It is used alongside the Warhammer Event Companion, whose mission sequence, layouts and pairing advice still apply except where noted here.

bonus.body: While an Alliance has control of this location, when a player in that Alliance draws **Battle Skill** cards, they can draw one additional card before choosing which to keep.
bonus.name: Battle-Tested

warZone.body: The battlefield edges that are not the Attacker's or Defender's battlefield edge are **canyon walls**. When a unit makes an **[gloss:ingress-move:ingress move]**, models in it cannot be set up within 6" of a canyon wall unless that model has FLY or [core:Deep Strike].
warZone.name: Canyon Walls

warZone.body: When a unit ends a move (excluding **[gloss:pile-in:pile-in]** and **[gloss:consolidation:consolidation moves]**) within 6" of a canyon wall, make a **[gloss:hazard-roll:hazard roll]** for that unit.
warZone.name: Rock Falls

bonus.body: While an Alliance has control of this location, when a player in that Alliance draws **Relic** cards, they can draw one additional card before choosing which to keep.
bonus.name: Munitions Vaults

warZone.body: In a player's Movement phase, that player can select one friendly unit in **[gloss:strategic-reserves:strategic reserves]**. That unit can make an **[gloss:ingress-move:ingress move]** this phase as if the battle round number was one higher than it actually is (note that this means it could arrive in the first battle round).
warZone.name: Landing Craft

warZone.body: (Once per battle) Each player can use the **Rapid Ingress** stratagem for 0CP.
warZone.name: Rapid Reinforcements

bonus.body: While an Alliance has control of this location, when a player in that Alliance draws **Battle Honour** cards, they can draw one additional card before choosing which to keep.
bonus.name: To the Victor

warZone.body: While a unit has the **[gloss:benefit-of-cover:benefit of cover]**, models in that unit have an **[gloss:invulnerable-save:InSv]** of 5+ against ranged attacks.
warZone.name: Defence Networks

warZone.body: When an INFANTRY unit **[gloss:remain-stationary:remains stationary]**, **[gloss:hidden:hidden]** models in that unit have a **[gloss:detection-range:detection range]** of 12" until the end of the turn.
warZone.name: Foxholes

bonus.body: While an Alliance has control of this location, the location for the next phase of the campaign is not randomly determined by the Warmaster. Instead, in the next Start Campaign Phase step, the players in that Alliance can choose what the next location will be (either by taking a vote or nominating one amongst them to choose).
bonus.name: Staging Post

warZone.body:
▪ All units have the SMOKE keyword.
▪ Models that are not within 24" of each other are not **[gloss:visible:visible]** to each other.
warZone.name: Shrouding Smoke

warZone.body:
▪ When an AIRCRAFT unit ends an **[gloss:ingress-move:ingress move]**, make a **[gloss:hazard-roll:hazard roll]** for that unit.
▪ When a FLYING unit ends a move in which it **[gloss:take-to-the-skies:took to the skies]**, make a **hazard roll** for that unit.
warZone.name: Ash Clouds

bonus.body: When an Alliance first takes control of this location, each player in that Alliance draws 1 random **Battle Skill** or 1 random Phase 1 **Battle Honour** card to keep.
bonus.name: Fresh Supplies

warZone.body:
In a player's Movement phase, that player can select one friendly **[gloss:strategic-reserves:strategic reserves]** unit to make a **Surgical Deep Strike**. If they do, while making an **[gloss:ingress-move:ingress move]** with that unit this phase, apply the following:

blocks.body:
An Armageddon campaign is split into 3 **campaign phases**, each of which consists of a number of battles. During each phase, the players will vie for control of a strategic **location**, before moving onto the next phase.
Taking control of the final location is key to achieving victory, but it is only part of the challenge. Each player also has a set of **Agendas** they must achieve during the campaign. Only commanders who can achieve military success while accomplishing these vital goals will achieve everlasting glory on Armageddon.
Designed to be used with any Chapter Approved mission deck, you can play this campaign with as many players as you wish to organise. While you can stretch a single deck across multiple players, we recommend that each player has a deck for themselves for convenience.
blocks.title: Armageddon Campaigns

blocks.body: Dominatus is best run with a **Warmaster**. They will take on the organisation of the campaign so that the other players can focus on playing games. A Warmaster can play in the campaign, but their primary role is to facilitate a smooth and enjoyable experience for all players involved. If such a heroic individual has not already volunteered themselves, the players can instead agree to take up the tasks of a Warmaster between themselves.
blocks.title: Warmaster

blocks.body: The deck contains 89 cards:

iconList.count: 35 cards — further categorised as **Battle Honour** cards (×11), **Battle Skill** cards (×9) and **Relic** cards (×15).
iconList.title: Upgrade deck

blocks.title: The Deck

blocks.body:
**Briefing cards** frame the narrative for each Alliance across the three campaign phases, listing the Agendas players can attempt depending on their Force Disposition and that of their opponent. On the reverse of each is a range of **Outcomes**, depending on how many **Narrative Points** you have gained.
**Location cards** represent strategically important zones on the planet Armageddon. Each one features a **location bonus**; if an Alliance takes control of a location, all players in that Alliance gain its location bonus for the remainder of the campaign. On the reverse of each are **war zone rules** that apply to every battle fought during the same campaign phase.
**Agenda cards** represent goals that you can attempt to achieve during each battle in a campaign phase. Each Alliance has a unique set of 9 Agendas: 3 for each campaign phase. One side lists the conditions that, if met, result in that player gaining Agenda Achieved cards; on the reverse is a Primary Mission, which tells you how to gain VP in the battle.

When a player gains an **Agenda Achieved** card, they take one corresponding to their Alliance. These do not have any effect until the end of a campaign phase. A player cannot have more than 3 Agenda Achieved cards at any one time.
Each card reads: "At the end of each campaign phase, the Alliance with the most **Agenda Achieved** cards is in **ascendancy**. At the end of campaign phases 1 and 2, shuffle your Alliance's **Relics** deck, then turn over a number of cards equal to the number of **Agenda Achieved** cards you have. Select one of the revealed **Relic** cards to keep, and return the others to the deck."
blocks.title: Agenda Achieved Cards

blocks.body:
Upgrade cards are acquired as the campaign unfolds. They represent special abilities that can improve the martial power of your warriors, and come in 3 types:
▪ **Battle Skill** cards: earned at the end of a battle.
▪ **Battle Honour** cards: earned at the end of a battle by the victor. There are 5 of these cards that can be earned during the first campaign phase, 5 during the second, and 1 during the third.
▪ **Relic** cards: the most powerful type of upgrade and the hardest to earn, unlocked by gaining Agenda Achieved cards. There are 5 unique Relic cards for each Alliance.
Some Upgrade cards list a **bonus effect** that applies when the upgrade is given to a particular type of model; such effects are always in addition to the normal effects listed on the card.
A player keeps all the Upgrade cards they gain, but they cannot have a duplicate of an Upgrade card.
blocks.title: Upgrade Cards

blocks.body: Before the campaign begins, the Warmaster should share a **Battle Schedule** with all players, informing them of the number of games each will play, and the army sizes they will need to muster. The default Battle Schedule below is designed to be played comfortably over the course of a weekend for players who can all muster a Strike Force sized army.
blocks.title: Preparing the Campaign

blocks.body:
The Warmaster will need to group all of the players into **Alliances**. A campaign must have an Oppressors Alliance and a Liberators Alliance. It can optionally have a Raiders Alliance as well. Alliances should be organised as evenly as possible, and based on the different factions players are using if possible. Players should play the same faction throughout the campaign.
These are guidelines, not requirements; if it suits the group better to organise Alliances differently, the Warmaster should do so.

boxes.body: Those who seek to free Armageddon, destroy the occupying forces and reestablish Imperial rule over the planet. The forces of the Imperium would be best suited to this Alliance.
boxes.title: Liberators

boxes.body: Those who wish to destroy Armageddon, slaughter its populace and watch the planet burn. The forces of the Orks are best suited to this Alliance.
boxes.title: Oppressors

boxes.body: The Raiders on Armageddon range from xenos warlords to Chaos renegades, all seeking to further their own agendas. This Alliance is best suited to those who carve their own path.
boxes.title: Raiders

blocks.boxesNote: Once players have been grouped into Alliances, it is time for the struggle for Armageddon to begin!
blocks.title: Alliances

blocks.body: Players start the first campaign phase using the sequence below. After completing phases 1 and 2, start the next campaign phase and repeat this sequence. At the end of phase 3, the campaign ends.
blocks.title: Start the Campaign

blocks.body:
At the start of each campaign phase, before any battles are fought, the Warmaster must:
▪ Roll one D6 to randomly select one of that phase's **Location** cards.
▪ Players read their Alliance's **Briefing** card for this phase.
▪ Players gather their Alliance's **Agenda** cards for this phase.
blocks.title: Start Campaign Phase

blocks.body:
Players from opposing Alliances now battle each other. The Warmaster can leave players to arrange games themselves, or organise days and times to help everyone play an equal number of games. In campaigns with a large number of players, each Alliance can be broken down into smaller subgroups that are then matched against each other.
To play a battle, the players generate a mission from any Chapter Approved mission deck (the Warmaster may curate this). The mission sequence is supplemented with the following rules.
### Determine Mission step
▪ Read aloud all **war zone rules** for that phase from your Location card — these apply to the upcoming battle.
▪ If both players wish to attempt Agendas in the battle, do not use the Primary Missions in your mission deck. Instead, after revealing Force Disposition cards, the players use their Alliance's current **Briefing** card and use the chart on it to compare their selected Force Disposition with that of their opponent. This combination will result in a specific **Agenda** card, which will state the Primary Mission to use in this battle.
blocks.title: Play Battles

blocks.body: If one or both players decline to attempt Agendas in a battle, determine Primary Missions as described in your mission deck, but only the player(s) that declined to attempt Agendas can score VP from that Primary Mission. A player that opted to attempt an Agenda cannot score VP from that Primary Mission and instead they use the Primary Mission on their Agenda card.
blocks.title: Declining Agendas

blocks.body:
### Declare Battle Formations step
▪ Each player can select up to 3 **Upgrade** cards they have earned during the campaign, and give each of those Upgrade cards to a different friendly unit until the end of the battle (a unit cannot have more than one Upgrade card).
### Determine Victor step
▪ Each player that opted to attempt an Agenda in the battle checks the conditions listed on their Agenda card. If these are met, that player takes the number of **Agenda Achieved** cards listed.
▪ During campaign phases 1 and 2: the victor randomly draws 1 **Battle Honour** card from that phase's deck, and their opponent randomly draws 1 **Battle Skill** card. If the battle is a draw, both players randomly draw 1 Battle Skill card.
▪ If a player gained 1 or more Agenda Achieved cards from the battle, they randomly draw 1 additional card of the same type at the same time. Each player then selects 1 of the drawn cards to keep, and returns the others to their respective decks.
▪ During campaign phase 3: the victor gains the phase 3 Battle Honour card, **Path to Conquest**, and players prepare for a final climactic battle!

At the end of each phase, each Alliance adds up the total number of Battle Honour cards gained from that phase and the number of Agenda Achieved cards its players have. Then, before starting a new phase or ending the campaign, resolve the following:
1. **Take Control** — the Alliance with the most Battle Honour cards gained during this campaign phase takes control of the current location. If a location bonus defines additional effects when an Alliance takes control, resolve these now. In the event of a tie, tied Alliances use the total number of Battle Honours gained over the course of the entire campaign as a tie-breaker; if there is still a tie, the Warmaster decides how best to resolve it.
2. **Determine Ascendancy** — the Alliance with the most Agenda Achieved cards is in **ascendancy**. This helps to determine the narrative Outcome of that phase. In the event of a tie, all tied Alliances are in ascendancy.
3. **Acquire Relics** — at the end of campaign phases 1 and 2, each player takes their Alliance's Relic cards deck and randomly draws a number of cards equal to the number of Agenda Achieved cards that player has. That player selects 1 of those Relic cards to keep and returns the others to the deck.
4. **Update Narrative Outcome** — the players read their Alliance's Outcome for that phase (on the reverse of their Briefing card). The Outcome depends on the number of **Narrative Points** your Alliance has earned this phase, as described on that card.
5. **Discard** — players discard all Agenda Achieved cards they have from previous phases.
blocks.title: End of Campaign Phase

blocks.body: Once the Outcomes of campaign phase 3 have been read, the campaign ends.
blocks.title: End Campaign

blocks.body:
The reverse of each Briefing card says how an Alliance earns Narrative Points that phase:
▪ Phases 1 and 2: gain 1 Narrative Point if your Alliance has control of this phase's Location, and gain 1 Narrative Point if your Alliance is in ascendancy (Outcomes for 2, 1 and 0).
▪ Phase 3: gain 2 Narrative Points if your Alliance has control of this phase's Location, and gain 1 Narrative Point if your Alliance is in ascendancy (Outcomes for 3, 2, 1 and 0).
blocks.title: Narrative Points

blocks.body:
The Warmaster can modify any of these rules to better suit the needs of their gaming group. While Dominatus is designed to be played over the course of a weekend, a Warmaster could use the deck to run a longer campaign by increasing the number of battles in a phase, remembering that phase 3 should consist of a single climactic final mission. It is also perfectly acceptable to vary the size-limit of players' armies as the campaign evolves, perhaps starting with smaller battle sizes in earlier phases and growing in subsequent ones.
Warmasters are free to change or introduce new rules to better fit their own narrative, perhaps allowing players to swap factions mid-campaign, or even change Alliance as new pacts are forged and traitors discovered — remembering that their role is to ensure everyone taking part has an enjoyable experience.
